description: The Open Grid Emissions dataset gives consumption-based and generation-based emission factors, individual generator data and data quality metrics for the US electric grid, with greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O and CO2-equivalent) and the criteria pollutants NOx and SO2. It is produced by the Open Grid Emissions Initiative of Singularity Energy, built on the same methodology and data inputs as EPA's eGRID, to meet the need for publicly accessible hourly grid emissions data for greenhouse gas accounting, policymaking, academic research and energy attribute certificate markets. Coverage is the United States, aggregated at balancing authority level, with annual and monthly data from 2005 to 2025 and hourly data from 2019. Files are selected from a data catalogue on Singularity's download page, the full archive is on Zenodo, and the pipeline code is on GitHub (version 0.8.0, commits to August 2026); the data are licensed under CC-BY-4.0 and the code under MIT, free of charge. Caveats: the newest early release year rests on preliminary EIA data and is published only at generator level until final data are available, releases come once a year in the autumn, and the pipeline pins Python 3.11. Simulation uses are capacity planning and optimisation studies that need emission factors and hourly generation profiles. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
